faq.q: What is the difference between baking soda and baking powder?
faq.a: Baking soda is just sodium bicarbonate and needs an acid in the recipe, like buttermilk, yoghurt or lemon. Baking powder already contains the acid, so it only needs liquid and heat.
asks: Can I use baking soda instead of baking powder?

faq.q: What does double-acting baking powder mean?
faq.a: It contains two acids: one that reacts as soon as it gets wet and one that reacts only when heated in the oven, so the batter rises twice.
asks: Why does baking powder fizz twice?

faq.q: Why does a cake sink if you open the oven too early?
faq.a: Before the sponge has set, cold air rushes in, the gas in the bubbles shrinks and the soft structure collapses.
asks: Why did my cake sink in the middle?

faq.q: Why does too much baking soda taste soapy?
faq.a: Leftover soda that has no acid to react with stays in the cake as a bitter, soapy-tasting base.
asks: Why does my cake taste bitter?

faq.q: Why add cornflour to baking powder?
faq.a: The starch soaks up moisture from the air so the acid and soda do not react in the tin before you use it.
asks: What is the starch in baking powder for?

facts: British chemist Alfred Bird created an early baking powder in 1843 because his wife could not eat eggs or yeast.
Heat in the oven also turns some water into steam, which helps a cake rise.

quiz.say: What gas makes a cake rise when you use baking powder?
quiz.show: What gas makes a cake rise when you use baking powder?
quiz.why: The acid and the baking soda react to make bubbles of carbon dioxide that expand in the oven.

wrong.0: Baking powder does not release oxygen.
wrong.1: No hydrogen is made; the gas is carbon dioxide.
